def compute_ranks(values):
    n = len(values)
    indexed = sorted(list(enumerate(values)), key=lambda item: item[1])
    ranks = [0.0] * n
    i = 0
    while i < n:
        j = i
        while j < n and indexed[j][1] == indexed[i][1]:
            j += 1
        # tie from i to j-1
        # ranks are 1-based indices: (i+1 + j) / 2
        avg_rank = ( (i + 1) + j ) / 2.0
        for k in range(i, j):
            ranks[indexed[k][0]] = avg_rank
        i = j
    return ranks

rank_y = compute_ranks(y_vals)
rank_x = compute_ranks(x_vals)

def pearson(u, v):
    n = len(u)
    mean_u = sum(u) / n
    mean_v = sum(v) / n
    num = sum((u[i] - mean_u) * (v[i] - mean_v) for i in range(n))
    den_u = sum((u[i] - mean_u) ** 2 for i in range(n))
    den_v = sum((v[i] - mean_v) ** 2 for i in range(n))
    return num / (den_u * den_v) ** 0.5

result = round(pearson(rank_x, rank_y), 6)
